acceptanceCriteria: ResourceFinalizationReceipt, ResourceFinalizationResult, ResourceFinalizationDisposition, and nested identity/state types use strict serde deny_unknown_fields and preserve repository/work-item/runtime bindings

A valid deleted receipt binds provider pull request number/url/head/base/merge identity, branch identity, worktree identity, before and after cleanup states, actor, authority source, reason, and timestamp

Deleted, retained, blocked, and unknown dispositions have explicit fail-closed invariants and failure/unknown codes; dirty, unmerged, protected, ambiguous, empty, invalid, or cross-repository/work-item data is rejected
Protocol validation exposes deterministic identity and idempotent replay checks without performing CLI, provider, filesystem, or branch deletion operations
Protocol unit tests cover valid round trip, unknown fields, empty/invalid values, foreign repository/work item, dirty/unmerged/protected/ambiguous states, and duplicate replay semantics
goal: Add a strict protocol-level Resource Finalization receipt and validation API with fail-closed disposition and replay semantics.
intent: Prevent merged Work Item branches and worktrees from being left unmanaged by introducing an auditable finalization receipt.
outOfScope: CLI commands, Runtime lifecycle integration, provider API calls, GitHub Actions, branch deletion, worktree deletion, and filesystem mutation
cockpit-repository, cockpit-cli, cockpit-mcp, documentation, and CI changes
